title: Retiming, Vanishing Labels, Kept Spaces, Cited Sentences & Honest Clocks
description: Five features that each delete a workaround: live WAAPI retiming, self-hiding anchors, kept whitespace, ::target-text and Temporal.

drops.title: Retime It While It Runs
drops.description: effect.updateTiming() changes duration, iterations, direction and easing on 25 running animations without restarting any of them.
drops.concept: A CSS animation is a declaration you replace; a Web Animations object is one you renegotiate with. Three scenes — a twelve-dot orbit, a five-card stagger and an eight-bar meter — share one timing object, and every panel control reaches into the live animations via updateTiming() or playbackRate instead of cancelling and re-creating them. The readout prints getComputedTiming() each frame so you can watch progress and currentIteration survive the change.

interaction.mouse: Drag the panel sliders to retime all 25 animations mid-flight; the dots never jump back to the start.
interaction.click: reverse(), finish(), pause and t = 0 act on every animation at once.
interaction.touch: Panel moves inline below the header on narrow screens and all controls stay tappable.

drops.title: Labels That Know When to Leave
drops.description: position-visibility lets an anchored pill hide itself the moment its anchor is clipped away by a scroller.
drops.concept: Anchor positioning glues a floating element to another element but says nothing about when it should stop existing, so scroll the anchor out of a clipping container and the label is stranded mid-air. position-visibility fixes it in one declaration, with anchors-visible and no-overflow. The drop detects the behaviour rather than trusting CSS.supports — the value parses in engines that then ignore it — and emulates it in script where it is missing, which is exactly the code the property deletes.
drops.source: modern.css by Naeem Noor — position-visibility reference

interaction.mouse: Drag the horizontal strip and the vertical rail; pills track their tile and leave with it.
interaction.click: The panel switches between always, anchors-visible and no-overflow so you can see the stranded-label bug.
interaction.touch: Both scrollers are touch-draggable with scroll snapping on the strip.

drops.title: The Spaces You Meant to Keep
drops.description: All five values of white-space-collapse on one indented poem, including break-spaces, where a line can break inside a run of spaces.
drops.concept: white-space always bundled two unrelated decisions — whether whitespace collapses and whether lines wrap — and white-space-collapse is the first half on its own. Five panels hold byte-for-byte identical source text under collapse, preserve, preserve-breaks, preserve-spaces and break-spaces, with a width slider that drives them to the wrap point where break-spaces stops behaving like anything that came before it. Values the engine has not implemented are flagged, so no panel is ever silently compared against itself.
drops.source: CSS Text Module Level 4 — White Space Collapsing (CSS WG Editor's Draft)

interaction.mouse: The width slider narrows every panel at once so you can watch the wrap points diverge.
interaction.click: Switch between four source samples and toggle whitespace-revealing marks.
interaction.touch: Panels stack to one column and the sample scrolls horizontally rather than squashing.

drops.title: Link to the Sentence, Not the Page
drops.description: A #:~:text= directive scrolls to a phrase that has no id, and ::target-text styles whatever the browser matched.
drops.concept: Text fragments turn a quote into an address: the fragment finds a string, scrolls it into view and marks it, with no cooperation from the document. ::target-text is the hook that makes that highlight yours rather than the OS selection colour. Chips here fire an exact match, a prefix-disambiguated pair, a start,end range and a deep match, with three highlight styles to switch between — plus a script fallback that finds and marks the phrase itself when the browser ignores the directive.
drops.source: web.dev — Boldly link where no one has linked before: text fragments

interaction.mouse: Hover the chips to see each directive, then fire one to scroll and highlight.
interaction.click: Each chip navigates to a text directive; the panel restyles ::target-text live and Clear resets.
interaction.touch: Chips wrap to multiple rows and the article scrolls normally.

drops.title: A Clock That Knows Where It Is
drops.description: A timezone meeting board built twice: on Temporal.ZonedDateTime, and on the Date arithmetic it replaces.
drops.concept: Date holds one number and has no idea what a day is. Temporal ships a ZonedDateTime that carries its zone, knows some local days run 23 or 25 hours and will tell you via hoursInDay. The component converts one instant across eight zones, steps it by calendar units, and then puts the two engines side by side on a clock-change date: adding a calendar day keeps the wall-clock time, while adding 86,400,000 ms moves the meeting by an hour for half its guests.
drops.source: OpenReplay — Replacing Date with the Temporal API

interaction.mouse: Change the date, time or home zone and the whole eight-zone board re-sorts by UTC offset.
interaction.click: Step by minutes, hours, days, weeks or months; panel presets jump to the EU and US clock changes.
interaction.touch: Native date and time inputs open the platform pickers; the board collapses to two columns.
